Re-apply the superior-haplotype rule with different settings

Source: R/association.r
hbr_regate.Rd

The pipeline calls a haplotype superior when four gates pass: a nominal significance threshold on the trait association (A), a permutation-based significance threshold (B), an effect-size minimum on the best-versus-runner-up comparison (C), and — when requested — an absolute trait value the best haplotype must reach (D). `hbr_regate()` recomputes which genes pass these gates under new thresholds, using the statistics already stored in the run, and reports how the call changes.

Usage

hbr_regate(
  x,
  alpha = NULL,
  min_cohens_d = NULL,
  require_fdr = NULL,
  trait_threshold = NULL,
  direction = NULL,
  ...
)

Arguments

x

A data.frame (legacy) or an `hbr_run` (new).

alpha

Significance threshold for the nominal and permutation gates, and for Benjamini-Hochberg FDR when `require_fdr = TRUE`. `NULL` inherits the run's stored value.

min_cohens_d

Minimum effect size for gate C. `NULL` inherits.

require_fdr

If `TRUE`, a gene is superior only if it also passes BH-FDR across all tested genes. `NULL` inherits.

trait_threshold

Absolute trait value gate D. `NA` removes the threshold. `NULL` inherits.

direction

Kept for backward compatibility with the legacy signature; ignored. The run carries its own direction.

...

Ignored.

Value

When `x` is a data.frame: a `data.table` with the recomputed columns. When `x` is an `hbr_run`: an object of class `hbr_regate` with elements `genes`, `settings`, `overlap` and `check`.

Details

Two calling conventions are supported.

**Data.frame input.** When `x` is a data.frame carrying at least a `P_value` column (and, for the effect-size gate, `Cohens_d` or `Hedges_g`), the function returns a copy of the table with `Adjusted_P`, `Significant_FDR`, `Significant_Nominal` and `Is_Superior` recomputed. This is the legacy behaviour and is fully backward compatible.

**Run input.** When `x` is an `hbr_run` (from [hbr_read_results()]) or anything that function accepts, all four gates are recomputed — including the permutation gate and, when the pipeline stored a trait threshold, the trait gate. Arguments left at `NULL` inherit the run's stored values, so the default call reproduces the pipeline exactly. The return is a classed object with the per-gene calls, the effective settings, the genes gained and lost versus the stored call, and a Jaccard overlap statistic.

The PCs the pipeline used and the Hedges correction cannot be changed here, because both alter the stored statistics; re-run the pipeline for that.

See also

[hbr_read_results()] to build the run input, [haplobreed_analysis()] for the pipeline that produced it.

Examples

# Legacy: data.frame input
summary_table <- data.frame(
  P_value  = c(0.001, 0.02, 0.5),
  Cohens_d = c(0.8, 0.4, 0.1))
hbr_regate(summary_table, alpha = 0.05, min_cohens_d = 0.3)
#>    P_value Cohens_d Adjusted_P Significant_FDR Significant_Nominal Is_Superior
#>      <num>    <num>      <num>          <lgcl>              <lgcl>      <lgcl>
#> 1:   0.001      0.8      0.003            TRUE                TRUE        TRUE
#> 2:   0.020      0.4      0.030            TRUE                TRUE        TRUE
#> 3:   0.500      0.1      0.500           FALSE               FALSE       FALSE

# New: hbr_run input re-applies all four gates
toy <- system.file("extdata", "hgsi_toy", "trait_YLD",
                   package = "HaploBreedR")
if (nzchar(toy) && dir.exists(toy)) {
  run <- hbr_read_results(toy)
  rg  <- hbr_regate(run, alpha = 0.01, min_cohens_d = 0.5)
  rg$overlap$gained
}
#> character(0)
